snn_assessment.opportunity: Native asynchronous sparse input and bounded causal timing could reduce active work and support local delayed updates; this is an implementation hypothesis.
snn_assessment.question: Can native sparse asynchronous observations and causally available timing support bounded temporal state and local delayed updates without a dense clock, packet duplication or expensive observer? Record opportunities, shared preprocessing/maintenance costs and missing empirical evidence. Event-driven ANN/non-spiking emulators may share these properties; no ANN-absent or SNN-exclusive advantage is claimed from metadata. Existing sufficient current/history/scalar controls and actual-update parity remain mandatory.
snn_assessment.required_evidence: Same native input/current, actual changed local writes, strongest causal non-spiking history controls and identical scalar replay; independently registered quality and complete CPU/work accounting.
snn_assessment.shared_costs: Input decoding, packet history/duplicate handling, time availability, state expiry and observer/maintenance work must be charged to every backend.

native_kitchen_on.basis: Published PIR message is a binary history array, not a raw scalar ON notification. Room renaming, bit conversion, packet expansion and backdating are outside the fixed contract.
